title: Tech Note: 4D and Google Charts API
author: Jean-Jacques BLEU, 4D Developer
featured_technology: Manual JSON string construction in 4D methods
Firebug browser console for JavaScript debugging

historical_commentary.text: Integrating third-party JavaScript charting libraries with 4D-sourced data via AJAX/JSON remains a completely valid general pattern, and Google Charts itself is still available today. However, the specific 4D-side implementation shown here — manually concatenating JSON text piece by piece in a method, and using 4D Web Server's basic On Web Connection-style request handling to build the response by hand — has been substantially superseded by 4D's later native JSON commands (JSON Stringify/Parse) and, more broadly, by 4D's built-in REST server (built on ORDA), which now provides structured JSON data endpoints without hand-rolled AJAX plumbing. The Firebug-based debugging workflow shown is also obsolete, since Firebug was discontinued years ago in favor of built-in browser developer tools.
related_updates: 4D's native JSON commands (JSON Stringify/JSON Parse, introduced 4D v15) replace manual string-concatenation JSON building
4D's built-in REST server (built on ORDA, 4D v16 R5+, 2017) provides structured JSON endpoints for exactly this kind of client-side charting scenario without hand-rolled On Web Connection code
Firebug was discontinued (2017) in favor of built-in Chrome/Firefox/Chromium developer tools
